question.problem: The inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{4}{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{1}{2})+1$ is ${f}^{-1}(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{4}{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{1}{2})+1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{4}{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{y}{4}-\frac{1}{2})+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{4}{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{y}{4}-\frac{1}{2})+1 \\ x-1 & =\frac{1}{4}{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{y}{4}-\frac{1}{2}) \\ 4x-4 & ={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{y}{4}-\frac{1}{2}) \\ {log}_{3}⁡(\frac{y}{4}-\frac{1}{2}) & =4x-4 \\ {3}^{{log}_{3}⁡(y/4-1/2)} & ={3}^{4x-4} \\ \frac{y}{4}-\frac{1}{2} & ={3}^{4x-4} \\ \frac{y}{4} & ={3}^{4x-4}+\frac{1}{2} \\ y & =4({3}^{4x-4}+\frac{1}{2}) \\ y & =4({3}^{4x-4})+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=4({3}^{4x-4})+2.$
